e485_one_day_cases.reading: no composing site in this repository names this member
the name states the run day because the composing expression reads the clock, so a one-day lag is the distance between the clock and the data

method_limits: the population is E485's member list (571 rows, 97 families); only members whose name carries exactly one literal date are matched, the rest are published as skipped

a naming site is a string-building expression (f-string, + concat, % format, .format) whose constant skeleton matches the member's basename with the date inside one dynamic gap -- a stem borrowed from another family is rejected by the full-name regex, not by the stem prefilter

when the family prefix is itself a variable, its literal values are resolved inside the same module; sites whose prefix never resolves to a literal are counted in sites_rejected_no_prefix_literal and sampled in rejected_sites
origin is resolved inside one module only: a symbol bound elsewhere is published as unresolved or parameter, never guessed across modules
several assignments of one symbol with disagreeing origins are published as mixed rather than picking the last one
a member with no site may have been written by a one-off script that has since been deleted; it is published as no_site, not as clock-named

the e485_compared_subset membership is E485's class field carried as a path list; the gate re-derives the counts from that list and the member spelling table, but cannot re-decide which members E485 compared

e485_compared_subset.source: members whose E485 class is same_day / payload_one_day_earlier / payload_one_day_later (the 402 comparable files)

title: For every dated face name in E485's population: which source composes the basename, which date symbol fills the date slot, and is that symbol the run clock or the payload's own cutoff?
